To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cytotoxic T-cell and a CD4+ T-helper response to a cancer testis antigen, sperm protein 17 (SP17), was detected in the peripheral blood of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma patients.
a CTL and CD4 T cell response to the immunogenic cancer testis antigen, sperm protein 17, was identified in a subset of diffuse large B cell patients.
we found a CTL and a Th response to Sp 17 in patients with DLBCL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of immunogenic cancer testis antigen-based vaccines for the treatment of diffuse large B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (DL-BCL-NHL).
the development and validation of immunogenic Sp17 peptides for use in immunotherapy of DLBCL and potentially other tumour types.
the development of novel immunotherapeutic approaches for DLBCL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Sp17 is a potential target for DLBLC patients.
Sp17 expression in DLBCL is associated with a CTL response, and a CD4+ response is also detected, and this is a potential immunotherapetic target.
the results presented in this paper support the hypothesis that Sp17 is an immunotherapeutic target in DLBCL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel Sp17 20-mer immunogenic CD4 Th epitope and confirmed the presence of a CTL response to Sp17 peptides in DLBCL.
the expression of Sp17 protein and Sp17 epitope recognition by the immune system are both present in DLBCL, suggesting Sp17 is an immunogenic target for immunotherapeutic approaches in DLBCL.
we found Sp17 expression in 31 DLBCL cases, 13 of which showed a CTL response to Sp17.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Sp17 and its immunogenicity in the context of MHC I and MHC II in DLBCL is a promising target for immunotherapy.
we have found a novel immunogenic 9-mer peptide that is presented by HLA-A2 and a novel immunogenic CD4 T-helper 20-mer peptide.
Sp17 is a promising candidate antigen for immunotherapy in DLBCL.
